findings.title: Unauthenticated Prometheus metric forgery via the request path
findings.root_cause: CorrelationIdMiddleware._stamping_send keys the RED counter on the raw, URL-decoded scope['path'] instead of the matched route template, and get_metrics f-string-interpolates that value into a Prometheus label with no escaping. %0A, %22 and %23 in the path therefore become real newlines, quotes and comment markers inside the exposition.

proof.secondary_dos: three GETs with a bare quote, a backslash and a bare %0A in the path produced 3 malformed lines out of 12, which makes a real Prometheus scrape fail wholesale
proof.persistence: module-level Counter -- poison survives until process restart
proof.unbounded_cardinality: route label is the raw path, so every distinct 404 path mints a new series; 3 requests to /random-aaa|bbb|ccc grew the counter from 4 to 7 entries with no eviction

findings.impact: An unauthenticated remote party can write arbitrary values into the platform's metrics and therefore into dashboards, alerting and this project's own runtime-SLO gate -- either fabricating SLO breaches or inflating the 200 counter to mask a real one. Plus a memory-exhaustion / TSDB-cardinality DoS from the same root cause.

findings.title: Attacker-controlled X-Request-ID and the raw path are written to the log sink verbatim
findings.detail: Redaction is registration-based by design (register_sensitive), and nothing sanitises the two inbound channels this story itself reads. X-Request-ID is taken verbatim, written to every log line for the request and reflected in the response header; the raw path is embedded in the access-log message.

proof.unbounded_length: a 4000-char X-Request-ID was accepted, reflected in the response header and written into the log line, producing a 4147-byte single record from a request whose response body is 59 bytes (~70x log amplification, no length cap)

findings.log_integrity_holds: X-Request-ID: 'a", "level": "CRITICAL", "message": "FORGED' was correctly escaped by json.dumps into one well-formed JSON line with no forged fields -- the JSON formatter is NOT injectable; only the metrics formatter is (HIGH-1)
findings.ac_coverage_gap: E15-S1-AC1's Given is 'an application payload', so the AC as written is satisfied and F001 is recorded as passing; but the story's stated business value ('keeps synthetic PAN, Aadhaar and salary content out of operational logs') and its Out-of-scope line ('must not write ... to any log sink') are not met for the header and path channels, and no AC covers them. Correcting this is a spec decision, not only a code one.

findings.title: /metrics exposes no duration metric, so half the declared SLO is unmeasurable
findings.proof: observability.slo declares p95_ms: 500, but /metrics exposes only http_requests_total. Every slo-check.js run in this evaluation reported "p95_ms": null. RED is Rate, Errors, Duration; Duration is absent.
findings.contributing_cause: routes.py notes /metrics 'is covered by no acceptance criterion' -- which is why the gap survived

findings.title: Untracked probe debris in backend/ breaks 'ruff check .'
findings.proof: cd backend && uv run ruff check . -> 92 errors, contradicting the context pack's 'All checks passed'. All 92 are in 14 untracked backend/_probe_*.py files (_probe_labelinj.py, _probe_metrics.py, _probe_redact.py, _probe_mem.py, ...) with mtimes inside the last 9 minutes and still being written during my run -- a concurrent evaluator instance's working-tree debris, not product code. git ls-files backend | grep _probe returns only tests/unit/test_health_probe.py. Scoped to tracked source, uv run ruff check src/ tests/ -> All checks passed!
findings.action: not a product defect, but the gate's lint result is untrustworthy until backend/ is cleaned, and these files must not be committed
